answer: In a vouching economy, a new key enters only when an established key spends one of its two invite slots per epoch and stakes its own earned reputation on it. Unvouched keys wait in a harbor pool, earning nothing until a beacon assigns a random sponsor. When an invitee fails a random audit, the penalty runs up the tree, so n clones need n honest sponsor slots and one catch can drain a whole canyon of linked stake. Earned reputation can't be bought in bulk. Hidden karst loops of one operator's keys vouching for each other show up as trees with no outside roots and get audited first.
